title: Cubs split pair of doubleheaders | Sports | codyenterprise.com
text:
Slow starts led to losses in the opening games of last weekend’s doubleheaders as the Cody Cubs wound up splitting the four games against teams from Montana.
The first doubleheader was on Saturday at home against the Gallatin Valley Outlaws. The Cubs offense didn’t produce much in a 12-4 loss for the opener, but the home team rallied for a 12-6 win in the second game at Simpson Stadium.
Going on the road Sunday afternoon, the Cubs again got off to a slow start in a 7-1 loss to the Miles City Mavericks. The Cubs offense then came to life in the late game as they gained the split with a 12-7 win.
“Our offense wasn’t clicking in the first game and the Outlaws got off to a hot start,” Cubs manager Beau White said. “It was kind of the same thing on Sunday, we just couldn’t get it going on offense. The guys then made nice comebacks to win the second games and we got a split in both doubleheaders. We turned it around with timely hits.”
Easton Hartley was the starting pitching for the Cubs in the first game against the Outlaws. He didn’t get much help from his offense and the early deficit led to a loss.
Despite three hits and four RBI from Kanin Phillips, the Cubs couldn’t catch up. The Outlaws scored a total of nine runs in their final four at-bats to get the win.
In the late game at home, the Cubs got the bats going and put up double-digit run totals. They scored a totals of seven runs in the third and fourth innings to take control of the game. Gaige Machen got the pitching win.
Phillips had another big game with the bat as he had a double, home run and four RBI. Russell Undeberg added to the offensive onslaught with a hit and three RBI.
“Kanin hit the ball well in both games and connected for some big hits in the late game,” White said. “He keeps coming up in big situations and delivers.”
After a loss in the opener on the road, the Cubs came back with hits throughout the lineup to win the late game on Sunday. Phillips and Machen each had two hits.
Westen Noziolek and Nick Horst also added key hits as the Cubs rallied late to get the win. This game was tied heading into the seventh inning. The Cubs then scored five runs in the top of the seventh to post the win and get the split.
“We had solid hitting from top to bottom throughout the lineup,” White said. “Even though we got off to another slow start, the guys stayed patient at the plate. We then executed on our offensive opportunities.”
Cody Cubs baseball (6-3 overall) plays road games this weekend at Glendive (Montana) and Sheridan.
